subject: Sustained-use & mixed-workload pricing proposal for MedAtlas RFP
messages:
From: Ellen Kane <ellen.kane@medatlas.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@medatlas.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFP question — mixed workload pricing and sustained-use discounts

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the RFP response last week. A few procurement clarifications for the commercial/pricing section before we move to final scoring:

1) MedAtlas runs a mixed workload: ~60% chat (low-latency), ~30% embeddings, ~10% bulk batch generation (long sequences). Can you provide a single-page summary that shows per-unit token/embedding list price plus an example blended effective rate at 1M/10M/50M tokens per month?

2) Do you offer sustained-use discounts that automatically tier down unit prices after a sustained commit (e.g., three months of consumption above a threshold)? If so, how do those interact with reserved committed capacity discounts and true-up mechanics?

3) For accelerated features (real-time streaming + GPU-optimized scores) you list an "accelerator surcharge" — is that billed as a flat premium per-token, a per-instance hourly surcharge, or both?

4) We need a rollover credit policy — if monthly consumption is under commit in a month, can credits roll forward and under what limits?

5) Finally, any SLA-backed credits for sustained latency misses on chat (p50/p95), and how do they affect overage billing?

If you can get a succinct commercial appendix back by EOD Thursday (Oct 1 PT) our procurement committee will review and likely move to final approval.

Best,
Ellen
Senior Procurement Manager
MedAtlas Health

Hi Ellen — thanks for the clear list. Summary answers below and I've attached a short commercial appendix and worked exemplar. Looping in Karthik (pricing) and Ben (sales/legal) for any fine points.

Top-line (short answers)
- Unit pricing: separate published list rates for Chat (per input+output token), Embeddings (per embedding vector) and Batch Generation (per token with sequence-length multiplier).
- Sustained-use discounts: yes — we offer an automatic 3-month sustained tier that reduces unit list price by up to 12% depending on threshold; it layers with committed capacity discounts but true-ups occur monthly against committed baseline.
- Accelerator surcharge: typically a per-hour per-pool surcharge for dedicated GPU instances + a nominal per-1000-token surcharge when using proprietary low-latency kernels; both apply when features are enabled.
- Rollover credits: unused committed tokens convert to "rollover credits" up to 30% of monthly commit and expire after 90 days.
- SLA credits: latency SLO misses accrue service credits (percentage of monthly invoice) applied against the current invoice; they do not retroactively change unit pricing or overage calculation.

I've included a worked example in the attached spreadsheet: blended effective rates at 1M/10M/50M monthly tokens under three configurations (self-serve hosted, dedicated reserved, private deployment). Please see the appendix for exact formulas.

Next steps: if this aligns with MedAtlas procurement expectations I can produce a redlineable SOW + pricing addendum for signature.

Thanks,

Marissa / Ben — quick notes on the spreadsheet I prepared for Ellen. I've highlighted the cells where legal or procurement will want firm language. Key details to confirm with MedAtlas:

- Sustained-use mechanics: we only auto-apply the sustained discount after 3 consecutive monthly periods above the threshold. The discount is applied prospectively (starting month 4) and reconciled with the committed baseline at true-up. If they terminate before month 4 the discount is not retroactive.

- Accelerator surcharge: propose two-part billing to keep modeling simple for procurement: (A) hourly surcharge for dedicated GPU pools (charged only when pool is provisioned), (B) usage surcharge of $0.60 per 1k tokens for real-time low-latency kernel paths. We can negotiate the per-1k token value as part of committed tiers.

- Rollover caps: 30% cap is standard but we can increase to 45% for 12+ month commitments (worth offering to move them toward annual reserved).

- Overage smoothing: propose a three-month smoothing window for true-ups (average consumption across months) rather than monthly spikes; optional for them to accept. Smoothed overages reduce short-term billing variability.

- SLA credits: keep as percentage credits (5% p30 for p95 misses beyond target) and explicitly separate from monetary overage calculations — credits apply to invoice, not to token unit rates.

I attached the draft appendix and a short one-pager describing the sustained-use algorithm (how thresholds, consecutive months, and cap interact). Happy to adjust numbers after Marissa/Ben decide what to present.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Pricing & Commercials — Redwood Inference
